status: frozen synthetic holdout for BNK-PDF-1 G20; sealed and committed before the product was run on any of its files
question: G18 and G19 gave the eligibility check the text items PDF.js builds, the reader's within-line overlap rule on them, and the reading by columns on them, measured on every sealed statement. Neither has met a writer it was not measured on. On statements from iText Core and from a Node application drawing with PDFKit, two writers not yet measured, with XLSX cashbooks from OpenSpout and write-excel-file, sealed with the complete check, does bank-statement-native-1 complete every eligible positive with no false automatic approval, and does the check before the seal say what the reader does with each file: its items, its overlap verdict, its reading by columns and each XLSX cashbook?

producers: iText Core 9.8.0 (Java 21; kernel and layout, AGPL, used outside the repository): a Java statement service drawing each page of the facts as one iText table of seven columns under the bank's heading, the footer placed at the page's foot; each line of text its own text object inside q and Q, the table's rules drawn after its text; Karla and Source Sans 3 created in iText's default simple encoding (WinAnsi), so that Karla is written as a simple TrueType subset and Source Sans 3, an OpenType CFF file, whole as a simple Type1C font, with no ToUnicode map; Roboto Mono and Lora in Identity-H as Type0 subsets with ToUnicode maps; no kerning or ligatures; English only, as iText Core lays out no right-to-left text without its commercial add-on

PDFKit 0.20.2 with fontkit 2.0.4 and bidi-js 1.0.3 (Node 22): a statement application drawing its own table, each page's content under PDFKit's flipped coordinate system; each line put in display order by bidi-js and cut into runs of one embedding level, each run drawn by its own text call and shaped by fontkit (Arabic joining, ligatures, kerning written into TJ arrays), a run of Arabic script given to fontkit reversed from its display order as fontkit sets it right to left, Arabic-Indic digits included; every font a Type0 subset with a ToUnicode map from each glyph's code points at its first use: Changa, Kufam, Baloo Bhaijaan 2, DM Sans and Inconsolata over TrueType outlines, Source Sans 3 over CFF outlines subset by fontkit as a CID-keyed CIDFontType0C program

OpenSpout 4.32.0 (PHP 8.3) for W03's typed XLSX cashbook: dates as Excel dates styled yyyy-mm-dd, amounts as numbers in riyals styled #,##0.00, the other amount cell empty, strings inline, an empty comments part; OpenSpout stamps docProps/core.xml with the clock's time and offers no setting for it, so a new render differs from the sealed file in that part alone
write-excel-file 4.1.1 (Node) for W10's text XLSX cashbook: every cell a shared string, amounts as plain decimals with two places, no docProps part at all
fonts: Karla, Source Sans 3 (OpenType CFF), Roboto Mono and Lora for iText
DM Sans, Source Sans 3 (OpenType CFF), Inconsolata (English) and Changa, Kufam and Baloo Bhaijaan 2 (Arabic, each one file holding its Latin letters and both kinds of digits) for PDFKit
the Google Fonts TrueType files packaged by @expo-google-fonts and Adobe's OpenType file from source-sans, used as installed, never converted, subset or merged here

independence.author: The same assistant wrote the product, the foundation, the oracle, the G6 to G17 holdouts, the fixes after them, the eligibility check with its G16 to G19 additions, and this holdout, and knew the reader's rules when designing the stories. iText Core, the PDFKit application and the two XLSX writers are new to the product; the author is not. This is not a blind holdout.
independence.oracle: audit/bank-statement-foundation/oracle.py, unchanged: it reads the printed lines in the facts, the cashbook CSV and the contract, never recipe or intent, and imports nothing from the generator or the product. expected.py only runs it story by story with each story's own period.
independence.verifier: pdfminer.six, a PDF reader unrelated to the product's pdf.js, finds every printed line of the facts on its own row with all its values, and every description's words in order across the rows the writer wraps it over, Arabic in reading order glyph by glyph; and MuPDF, with the CFF charset read for a CID-keyed font, finds no glyph drawn as .notdef (verify.py, with its own self-test of planted changes, two changed XLSX cashbooks, and a letter planted as .notdef in each kind of font the two writers embed here: iText's simple TrueType, simple Type1C and Type0 TrueType fonts, PDFKit's Type0 TrueType and Type0 CFF fonts).
independence.eligibility: audit/bank-statement-eligibility/eligibility.py, run on the frozen files before the seal with MuPDF, the raw content streams and the Python standard library, never the product: every refusal the reader declares that it can check, the text items as PDF.js builds them and the overlap within a line on them (G18), the reading by columns on those items (G19), each font's ToUnicode map as the prepared PDF.js reads it (G15), each XLSX cashbook as the product reads it (G16), the rules each statement exercises, and the decision story's case and outstanding item. Its report, ELIGIBILITY.json, is sealed and bound to the PDF hashes.
independence.generator: stories.py is a tenth lineage: an online retailer's operating account driven by a PCG32 generator (XSH RR); nothing is imported from the foundation's stories.mjs or from the G6 to G17 holdouts. common.py, expected.py and check_export.py are copied from G17, verify.py, check_seal.py and test_seal.py adapted from G17's.
independence.drafts: While the stories and writers were drafted, their PDFs and workbooks were read with pdfminer.six, MuPDF (text, glyph ids and page images), the eligibility check and its cashbook check only. No script that reads a file with the product's reader was run on any draft (DEV-61).
independence.notTuned: No product code changed between the start of G20 and the seal, and the product read none of these files.

eligibility.decided: before any product run on these files
eligibility.why: Every statement stays inside the contract: its headings, labels, footer, line kinds, number and date formats and matching policy; every cashbook keeps the six declared headings on one sheet. The writer, font, table style, geometry, period, furniture and story are what the contract leaves open. The eligibility check found nothing in any of the twelve statements that the reader declares a reason to refuse, built every page's PDF.js items with no overlap in a line, read every one by its columns and every font's ToUnicode map as the prepared PDF.js reads it, and read both XLSX cashbooks as the product reads them, every entry (ELIGIBILITY.json). So a refusal of a positive is not a correct one unless it is for a reason no check before the seal covers, which the report then names.
eligibility.exercised: As ELIGIBILITY.json counts them: dates read with their segments reversed in the Arabic statements with Arabic-Indic digits (W07, W08, W12); values placed in their columns by the end edge of their heading in the English statements whose headings are right-aligned and in the Arabic statements whose amounts stand at the left edge (W07, W12); DR after each amount in W03; the continuation in W08; word parts in the English statements; W03's cashbook read with typed amounts and dates, W10's as text.
draftFindings: PDFKit names each glyph in its ToUnicode map by the code points of the glyph's first use. A font that draws several letters with one glyph gives a text layer naming other letters: Mada draws ب, ت, ث, ن and ي on one dotless form with their dots as marks, and Scheherazade New draws أ and إ as alef and hamza, so the first drafts of W08 and W09 read 'النحر' for 'البحر' and 'الأفتتاحي' for 'الافتتاحي'; verify.py found it. Every Arabic text of the stories was then drawn by the application in eleven Arabic families and read back with pdfminer.six: Changa, Kufam, Baloo Bhaijaan 2, Lemonada and Marhey right in all 208 words; Zain wrong in 3; Mada, Mirza, Reem Kufi, Scheherazade New, Lateef and Harmattan wrong in 15 to 83. W08 was moved to Kufam and W09 to Baloo Bhaijaan 2. A text layer naming the wrong letters holds no facts any reader can verify; it is recorded here, not sealed.

iText broke W04's long description after the hyphen inside 'late-June', so that the file cannot tell 'late-June' from 'late- June'; verify.py found the word out of order. The description was reworded without a hyphenated word.
In Roboto Mono at 7.2 points W03's overdrawn balances wrapped their DR onto a second line of the balance cell. The monospaced type is set at 6.4 points.
verify.py read the document information after closing the file and failed on iText's statements, which write those strings as objects of their own; it now reads them while the file is open.

verify.py found a .notdef glyph by MuPDF's glyph id 0; in a CID-keyed CFF font, as PDFKit writes Source Sans 3, MuPDF gives the CID instead, and a CID the font's charset lacks is drawn as .notdef unseen. The check now reads the charset of such a font, and its self-test plants a letter whose CID the charset no longer holds.

iText draws its subset prefixes and its document identifier itself, and OpenSpout stamps docProps/core.xml with the clock, with no setting for either: two renders differ in those bytes alone. They are left as the writers write them and recorded here.

The drafts were read with pdfminer.six, MuPDF, the eligibility check and its cashbook check only; the font measurement above read with pdfminer.six PDFs the application drew from the stories' Arabic texts. No script reading with the product's reader ran on any draft (DEV-61).

browserDecision.why: The browser run accepts the first acceptable case of one story and the export checker's self-test alters that story's workbook. W01 has a case the page accepts (date-gap) and items outstanding on both sides, so every alteration has a target; ELIGIBILITY.json checks it. If the product refuses W01, the next of W07 (date-gap, an item outstanding) and W02 (amount-date-suggestion, an item outstanding) it does not refuse is decided.

attribution.what: After the first run, the same package is run on the product as it was before G17's fix (06ec495: a space glyph the writer drew was not yet a space whatever the kerning) and recorded beside it, so that a difference says whether that rule changed the outcome on writers it was not measured on; both writers here draw their spaces as glyphs. It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

rules: rectangle traced back to its start
ablation.what: After the first run, on the commit it ran on, each rule is switched off in a private copy of the product, one at a time, and the package run again: a positive that completes with every rule and not with one off needed it. It is a diagnostic, not a second result.

measures.reading: Every printed line read from the PDF equals the facts: kind, page, dates, reference, amounts, balances; descriptions and continuation text after NFKC and whitespace normalisation.
measures.result: The matching result, in the facts' keys, equals EXPECTED.json: automatic pairs, review groups with their reasons, both outstanding sides, timing, and held statements with their counts.
measures.capacity: Eligible positives whose result equals EXPECTED.json from upload through matching, save, restore and Excel in the browser.
measures.falseAutomatic: Automatic pairs that EXPECTED.json does not hold, over all twelve statements. Must be zero.
measures.held: A held statement is held whole, with the oracle's status, and nothing in it approved, suggested or called outstanding.
measures.refusal: A positive the product refuses, or holds without the oracle holding it, is a failed positive, never a correct abstention.
measures.cashbookAgreement: For W03 and W10, the product's reading of the XLSX cashbook equals the CSV's, and equals what the eligibility check read before the seal.
measures.prediction: After the first run, the check before the seal against the reader on these files: PDF.js's items and the overlap verdict (measure_items.mjs), the reading by columns and the rules counted (measure_columns.mjs), each XLSX cashbook (measure_cashbook.mjs), recorded with the commit they ran on.

afterRun: Results are recorded as they come, with the commit they ran on. A fix made after seeing them turns this set into regression for that fix; a new claim of generalisation needs a new holdout.
